newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - UK BUSINESS NEWS - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - UK BUSINESS NEWS - Jan 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- IVORY SHRUGS OFF TALK OF TAKEOVER

Colin Hook, managing director of Ivory & Sime, has dismissed speculation that the Edinburgh-based fund management group may be vulnerable to a takeover after a sharp fall in its share price. Hook has been criticised for his week-long silence after the defection of four fund managers. He says there is no comparison with its Scottish rival Dunedin, where a walkout by 12 managers left the group open to a takeover by Edinburgh Fund Managers.
-- DRINK GROUP LAUNCHES FIGHTBACK

Drinks group Matthew Clark, whose shares collapsed last year when it warned that alcopops had undermined sales of Diamond White, K and Babycham, has launched a fightback by promising to lift its advertising budget from 1.7 million to 10 million stg. The marketing strategy helped lift shares by 29. Chief executive Peter Aikens said five million stg will be spent on advertising the Blackthorn cider range.
-- KLM FACES EURO FINE OVER PACT

Dutch national airline KLM is facing the threat of fines from the European Commission for failing to move fast enough in providing details of its link-up with Northern Airlines. Commission officials will reach a decision today on whether to introduce the fine mechanism. The warning represents a tougher approach by the commission towards airline alliances. KLM says it is having discussions with the commission but had not received any formal notice of a fine.
THE TIMES
-- OPTIMISM ON RATES FEEDS MARKET FEVER

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is to stand firm against calls for higher interest rates when he meets Eddie George, Governor of the Bank of England. This has led to shares racing to a record high, with the FT-SE 100 index of leading shares rallying strongly for the second successive day. The buying came on renewed optimism about the outlook for base rates. Optimism was reinforced by news of a lower than expected rise in America consumer prices.
-- NATIONAL EXPRESS CHIEF RESIGNS

Ernest Patterson, chief executive of bus operator National Express, has resigned after only five months in the post, putting it down to "cultural differences". Finance director Colin Child denied there had been any disagreement about the group's acquisition strategy. He is set to receive a payout of 250,000 stg. His place will be taken by Phil White, former head of West Midland Transport, which National Express bought 18 months ago.
-- BA CONFIDENT OF AMERICAN LINK-UP

Chief executive of British Airways, Bob Ayling, has insisted the alliance with American Airlines will go ahead, despite disagreements with the EC. Ayling says the European Competition Commissioner, Karel van Miert, is wrong to suggest, in a letter to Ian Lang, president of the Board of Trade, that a combined group would restrict the competition between America and the UK.
His remarks have raised questions about who will ultimately have the say on approval of the alliance.
THE GUARDIAN
-- MORGAN HIT BY NEW CRISIS

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management has suspended Nicola Horlick, head of its UK pension fund business, over a "potential breach of contract". She has been suspended from her duties for attempting to take some of her colleagues to a rival investment bank, believed to be ABN Amro. Pension advisers have warned Horlick's departure could mean disaster for MGAM and its 18 billion stg pension fund business, with a loss of institutional clients.
-- JOBLESS FIGURES POSE INFLATION THREAT

Figures from the Centre for Economics and Business Research show unemployment falling half as rapidly as it did in November, threatening the Government's inflation target and pushing up interest rates. The centre argues that the 2.5 per cent inflation target is not compatible with the 40,000 average monthly decline in the number of people out of work and claiming benefit.
-- HOUSE PRICE SURGE IS LED BY LONDON

According to a regional survey by the Halifax Building Society, house prices in London are rising by 15 per cent over the past year and spearheading a recovery across Britain. The mortgage lender is dampening speculation about a 1980s-style house price boom due to fears that the Government would have to act swiftly against signs of overheating in the market, through sharp interest rate rises.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SOUTHAMPTON SHINES AS FOOTBALL CLUBS FLEX FOR ACTION

Shares in Secure Recruitment, the property development and healthcare group that merged with Southampton, the Premier League football club, have soared on their return to the stock market. Chairman, Rupert Lowe, denied suggestions the club had been bought too cheaply, however, analysts say the 10 million stg reverse takeover, valuing Southampton at the equivalent of its annual turnover, was far less when compared to other Premiership club Sunderland, whose floated shares are already trading on over eight times sales.
-- CIRO CITTERIO TAKES DUNN AND CO INTO THE FOLD

Men's outfitters, Dunn & Co, has been rescued from receivership, with debts of 6.4 million stg, by fashion retailer Ciro Citterio, who bought the group for an undisclosed sum. The deal will save 500 jobs as the purchaser pledged to maintain the group's 130 stores, its warehouse and head office. However, the Dunn & Co name will only survive in a diminished form, as some of the shop names will be changed to Ciro Citterio.
-- MORE PROJECT DELAYS HIT BABCOCK SHARES

Shares in Babcock International, the engineering to dockyard group, have slipped by four pence after work on a big Australian project for Hanson's SCM chemicals operation had been deferred to 1998. The group said the delay would not have any significant impact on this year's results, but would reduce revenues for the year to March 1998 by around eight million stg. Some of this will be offset by a 10 million stg contract with British Chrome and Chemical to build a new chromic acid plant on Teeside. BMC +44-171-377-1742 END
